byron.basis: points races only (race_type_id = 1: excludes the Clash, Daytona Duels and All-Star races); see describe_data

excitement.basis: points races only (race_type_id = 1: excludes the Clash, Daytona Duels and All-Star races); see describe_data
excitement.sql: SELECT track_type, count(*) AS races, round(avg(lead_changes), 1) AS avg_lead_changes, round(avg(cautions), 1) AS avg_cautions, round(avg(margin_of_victory), 3) AS avg_margin_of_victory, round(avg((margin_of_victory < 0.1)::INT) * 100, 1) AS pct_photo_finish FROM race_excitement GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg_lead_changes DESC

definitions.points race: race_type_id = 1. Excludes the Clash, Daytona Duels, All-Star Race and All-Star Open (race_type_id = 2). Every season stat (wins, top 10s, average finish) counts points races only.
definitions.pole: starting_position = 1 in a points race (includes poles set by metric when qualifying is canceled).
definitions.DNF: a points-race finish whose finishing_status is not 'Running' (Accident, Engine, DVP and other mechanical or damage reasons). A blank status is treated as unknown, not a DNF.
definitions.average finish: mean finishing_position over points races started.
definitions.track type: one of superspeedway (Daytona, Talladega, and Atlanta since its 2022 drafting reconfiguration), intermediate, short_track, one_mile_flat, large_flat, road_course (includes street courses). A documented judgment call; see the tracks table.
definitions.margin of victory: seconds between first and second at the finish; null when the feed gives none.
definitions.season: race_season; 2022-2026 are the Next Gen car's first five seasons.

tools.name: describe_data
tools.description: Start here. Lists the tables and columns, the seasons covered (2022-2026 Cup Series), the six track types and the business definitions every answer must follow: wins, top 10s, poles, DNFs and averages count POINTS RACES ONLY (the Clash, Daytona Duels and All-Star races are excluded).

tools.name: driver_season_stats
tools.description: One driver's points-race season: starts, wins, top5s, top10s, poles, dnfs, laps_led, avg_finish, avg_start, points. Accepts a full or last name; returns an error listing the options if the name is ambiguous (e.g. 'Dillon').

tools.name: excitement_by_track_type
tools.description: How competitive races are by track type: average lead changes, cautions, margin of victory (seconds) and the share of photo finishes (margin under 0.1 s), for points races, optionally for one season.

tools.name: race_result
tools.signature: (season: int, race: str, top_n: int = 40) -> dict
tools.description: Finishing order of one points race, by track name, race name or YYYY-MM-DD date. Tracks that host two races a season (e.g. Daytona, Talladega, Martinsville) return an error listing both; then ask by race name or date.

tools.name: run_sql
tools.description: Read-only SQL over DuckDB for anything the other tools don't cover. One SELECT/WITH statement; writes are refused. Use the points_results view (points races only, with win/top5/top10/pole/dnf flags and track_type) for stats, so answers match the official definitions.

tools.name: season_leaders
tools.signature: (season: int, stat: str = wins, top_n: int = 10) -> dict
tools.description: Leaderboard for one season (points races only). stat: wins, top5s, top10s, poles, dnfs, laps_led, points, starts, avg_finish or avg_start (the two averages rank lowest first and require 10+ starts). Ties are broken alphabetically, so check the stat value before calling someone the sole leader.

tools.name: top10_probability
tools.signature: (driver: str, track: str, start_pos: int) -> dict
tools.description: Model estimate of the chance a driver finishes in the top 10 from a starting spot at a track, using his form entering the most recent race in the data. Calibrated on 2026 races held out from training; see the site for accuracy. A forecast, not a certainty.

tools.name: track_history
tools.description: Points-race winners at a track since a season (inclusive) and the average lead changes, cautions and margin of victory there. 'Charlotte' means the oval; ask for 'Charlotte Motor Speedway Road Course' for the Roval.
